summary: L004 executed successfully and passed the fixed G01 positive-Tc guard (8.5017 K <= 8.8322 K), but it was not an eligible improvement. Its pooled weighted OOF MAE was 7.8380 K versus A05's 7.7526 K, a deterioration of 0.0854 K rather than the required gain of at least 0.01 K. Relative to A05, reported-zero MAE worsened from 6.0806 K to 6.3634 K, while positive-Tc MAE improved marginally from 8.5051 K to 8.5017 K and high-Tc MAE was unchanged at 28.8502 K. Thus, retaining only the cu_o expert produces a subgroup tradeoff and shows that A05's pooled advantage requires the other-route specialization or its combination with cu_o; it is not explained by cu_o specialization alone.
next_focus: Because the continuation minimum remains pending, run the complementary untried A05 ablation: composition input, chemistry routing, global extra_trees/raw, and only an other-route extra_trees/raw expert, with cu_o and fe_anion falling back globally. Comparing this directly with G01, L004, and A05 will isolate whether the large other partition supplies A05's improvement by itself or whether the cu_o and other experts interact additively. The hypothesis is falsified as an eligible improvement if pooled weighted OOF MAE is not below 7.742598770753422 K or positive-Tc MAE exceeds 8.832165507919859 K; subgroup gains without both conditions remain tradeoffs.
limitations: All measurements are adaptive development evidence from reused fixed-group training OOF folds, not independent validation or proof of generalization.
Chemistry routes are operational composition partitions rather than verified physical material families.
The cu_o route has only 66 groups and its high-Tc subgroup has 18 groups, so route-level comparisons may be unstable.
The observed counterexamples show unresolved cu_o ambiguity, with large overpredictions for reported-zero materials and large underpredictions for high-Tc materials.
The allowed menu still contains untried configurations, and these results do not establish or identify new superconductors.
